title: How Sure Can One Case Make You?
scopeNote: This keeps the sequential reveal set against a running record of the learner's own stated confidence, which is the mechanism. Three of the original's six complications are kept, chosen because they fail in three different ways. The other three, the claim-sorting exercise separating single-case from population claims, and the full rating trace stay in the longer version.
summary: One fictional case, one localisation claim, and the learner's own confidence in it rated before each of three complications arrives. Their line is drawn against a ceiling that only ever falls.
learningObjectives: Explain why lesion evidence speaks to necessity rather than to what tissue does.
Name three specific reasons a region-to-symptom inference can go wrong.
Distinguish a claim about one person from a population claim about a region.
Explain why vascular co-occurrence does not average away as a lesion sample grows.
Separate deficits attributable to damaged tissue from those attributable to swelling and diaschisis.
interactionTypes: a confidence rating made before each complication is seen
three complications revealed one at a time
a live trace of the learner's ratings against a falling evidence ceiling
a shaded band marking confidence the evidence does not support
a summary that reads the learner's own trace back to them
privacy: Nothing is collected, stored or transmitted. Every rating is held in the browser and is gone when the page is closed.
accessibilityNotes: Keyboard operable throughout, with the confidence rating a native range input carrying a live value output. The chart carries a description giving the ceiling at every stage, every rating the learner has made, and what the shaded region means, so nothing depends on reading the lines. The learner's line and the ceiling differ by dash pattern and end label as well as by colour. Each complication is announced through a polite live region as it arrives. Nothing is timed and there is no motion.
dataStatus: Fictional. Mrs D does not exist, the scan findings are invented, and nothing here is a diagnosis or a description of any real person.
simulationNotes: The ceiling is a teaching device rather than a calculation, and the caution says so: no formula turns three complications into a number and a different neuropsychologist would draw the line elsewhere. What is not arbitrary is the direction, since every complication removes support and none adds any. The rating must be made before the next complication is shown, because the whole mechanism is watching your own number sit above a line that keeps falling. All four outcome patterns are given their own wording, including staying below the ceiling throughout, which is described as unusual rather than as correct.
readmeTopic: why a single lesion case supports much less localisation inference than it feels like
